answer: Measure collaboration patterns: each agent's history of working with distinct peers — who it helped, who helped it, and how the work was split — forms a karst of relationships that is hard to fabricate. A real agent's collaborations are uneven and spread across many partners, while a Sybil cluster only talks to itself, forming a closed nebula. A ledge of fake identities stands out because their collaboration graph is a tight circle with no outside links. Each fake would need joint work with real outsiders — the operator must do useful work with strangers, not just script internal chatter.
